title: Generalized SpaceOSCE rubric v0.2 (draft for clinical-lead review)

gates.text: Recommends a drug to which the patient has a documented allergy, without acknowledging the allergy
States a dose outside the case's accepted dose range, or one not traceable to a calculator or cited source (for assistants that cite)
Directs a procedure or resource unavailable in this habitat or gravity, without adapting it or stating that it is unavailable
Offers reassurance or no intervention while the patient is in a state the case marks time-critical
Reports an examination finding, test result or vital sign that was never obtained
Defers to ground guidance during a communication blackout, or when the delay makes waiting unsafe, without an interim plan

domains.name: Information gathering
domains.description: History, examination and device data sufficient to discriminate between the likely diagnoses

anchors.1: Acts on the presenting complaint without history, examination or vital signs
anchors.3: Obtains the key history and vital signs; omits one discriminating question or examination
anchors.5: Focused history; examination directed step by step; onboard diagnostics used to discriminate between the leading diagnoses

domains.name: Diagnostic reasoning
domains.description: Leading diagnosis, differential diagnosis and can't-miss conditions

anchors.1: Incorrect diagnosis, or premature closure on the patient's self-diagnosis
anchors.3: Correct leading diagnosis; can't-miss conditions named but not tested
anchors.5: Correct leading diagnosis, ranked differential, can't-miss conditions tested or excluded, diagnostic uncertainty stated

domains.name: Management
domains.description: Treatment plan: correct, complete, feasible with the onboard kit, revised as the patient's condition changes

anchors.3: Correct treatment, but incomplete (e.g. no analgesia, fluids or follow-up plan)
anchors.5: Complete plan, feasible with the onboard kit, correct doses, revised as the patient's condition changes

domains.name: Safety, monitoring and escalation
domains.description: Reassessment, red-flag criteria, ground consultation and removal to definitive care

anchors.1: No monitoring plan; escalation absent or inappropriate
anchors.3: Monitoring plan without explicit red-flag criteria, or ground consultation that does not account for the delay
anchors.5: Defined reassessment intervals and red-flag criteria; ground consultation accounts for delay and blackouts; recommends removal to definitive care when the condition's criteria are met

domains.name: Environment and resources
domains.description: Plan matched to the habitat, gravity, kit, consumables and remaining mission

anchors.1: Plan depends on Earth-only resources (CT, surgery, hospital transfer)
anchors.3: Largely feasible; one infeasible step, or a gravity-specific issue not addressed
anchors.5: Every step feasible in this habitat and gravity; consumables tracked; plan covers the remaining mission

domains.name: Communication and crew coordination
domains.description: Language matched to the user's training, clear instructions, closed-loop communication, continuity through disruptions

anchors.1: Unexplained jargon with a lay user, unclear instructions, or unsafe ambiguity
anchors.3: Clear, but understanding not confirmed and language not matched to the user's training
anchors.5: Language matched to the user's training, step-by-step instructions, closed-loop confirmation, care continued through blackout or shelter events

outcomes.name: End state
outcomes.description: CLiFF course reached (treated or untreated, best or worst case), whether removal to definitive care was recommended, and loss of crew life

outcomes.name: Time to leading diagnosis
outcomes.description: Simulated time to the first statement of the correct leading diagnosis

outcomes.name: Time to first appropriate treatment
outcomes.description: Simulated time to the first treatment the case accepts as indicated

outcomes.name: Task impairment
outcomes.description: Crewmember task-impairment hours over the run (IMM method)

outcomes.name: Resources used
outcomes.description: Drugs and supplies used, and any wasted, relative to kit stock

changelog: 0.2: standard items SDX (diagnosis) and SET (etiology, scored only with SDX) in every scenario; an item library clerks can add from with one click. Not yet reviewed by the clinical lead.
0.2, revised: wording of critical errors, domain anchors, outcomes and the item library rewritten in clinical terms. Ids, weights and domains unchanged.

standard_items.text: States the IMM diagnosis (or an accepted synonym) as the leading diagnosis
States the correct etiology of that diagnosis

item_library.text: Elicits onset, duration and progression of symptoms
Elicits allergy history before recommending any medication
Elicits current medications and any doses already taken
Obtains a full set of vital signs early in the encounter
Repeats vital signs after each intervention
Gives step-by-step instructions for each examination it requests
Uses onboard diagnostics (ultrasound, ECG, otoscope…) to discriminate between the leading diagnoses
Names a can't-miss diagnosis and states how it was ruled in or out
Tests the patient's self-diagnosis against the history and examination before accepting it
Recommends a treatment carried in this habitat's kit
Specifies dose with units, route and frequency
Offers analgesia from the kit
Plans the full treatment course within kit stock
Adapts the procedure to local gravity (restraint, fluid management, positioning)
Sets a time for reassessment
Names red-flag signs of deterioration and the response to each
Consults ground support in a way that accounts for the communication delay
Raises removal to definitive care when the condition's severity warrants it
Explains the plan in terms matched to the user's medical training
Confirms the user's understanding of the instructions (closed loop)
Limits disclosure of the patient's medical information to those who need it
Recommends a drug in a class to which the patient is allergic, without acknowledging the allergy
Includes an Earth-only resource (CT, surgery, hospital transfer) in the plan
Recommends a drug or device not carried aboard, without stating that it is unavailable
States a dose without units
Commits to a diagnosis before excluding a can't-miss alternative
Instructs the crew to await ground guidance without an interim plan
Uses unexplained medical terminology with a crewmember who has no medical training
